name: Question 20
problem:
The acceleration $a$ at time $t$ of a particle $P$ moving in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
a(t)=⟨48(2t+1)^{2},\,-6⟩.
$$

Given that the particle is at the position $(2,-1)$ and has velocity $⟨8,\,5⟩$ when $t=0,$ calculate the position vector of $P$ at time $t.$

$r(t)=⟨${{field-1}}$,\,-3{t}^{2}+5t-1\,⟩$
worked_solution:
To compute the position vector, we need to integrate the velocity vector. To find the velocity vector, we first need to integrate the acceleration vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨48(2t+1)^{2},\,-6⟩\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int 48(2t+1)^{2}\,\text{d}t,\,\int (-6)\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨8(2t+1)^{3}+{C}_{1},\,-6t+{C}_{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that $v(0)=⟨8,5⟩.$ Substituting $t=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(0) & =⟨8(1)^{3}+{C}_{1},\,-6(0)+{C}_{2}⟩ \\ ⟨8,5⟩ & =⟨8+{C}_{1},\,{C}_{2}⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

so, we must have ${C}_{1}=0$ and ${C}_{2}=5.$ Therefore, the velocity vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t)=⟨8(2t+1)^{3},\,-6t+5⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we integrate the velocity vector to obtain the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨8(2t+1)^{3},\,-6t+5⟩\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int 8(2t+1)^{3}\,\text{d}t,\,\int (-6t+5)\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨(2t+1)^{4}+{C}_{3},\,-3{t}^{2}+5t+{C}_{4}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that $r(0)=(2,-1).$ Substituting $t=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r(0) & =⟨(1)^{4}+{C}_{3},\,0+0+{C}_{4}⟩ \\ ⟨2,-1⟩ & =⟨1+{C}_{3},\,{C}_{4}⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

so, we must have ${C}_{3}=1$ and ${C}_{4}=-1.$ Therefore, the position vector of $P$ at time $t$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨(2t+1)^{4}+1,\,-3{t}^{2}+5t-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

To compute the position vector, we need to integrate the velocity vector. To find the velocity vector, we first need to integrate the acceleration vector: v(t)=∫a(t)dt=∫⟨48(2t+1)2,−6⟩dt=⟨∫48(2t+1)2dt,∫(−6)dt⟩=⟨8(2t+1)3+C1,−6t+C2⟩

We can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that v(0)=⟨8,5⟩. Substituting t=0, we get v(0)=⟨8(1)3+C1,−6(0)+C2⟩⟨8,5⟩=⟨8+C1,C2⟩, so, we must have C1=0 and C2=5. Therefore, the velocity vector is v(t)=⟨8(2t+1)3,−6t+5⟩.

Now, we integrate the velocity vector to obtain the position vector: r(t)=∫v(t)dt=∫⟨8(2t+1)3,−6t+5⟩dt=⟨∫8(2t+1)3dt,∫(−6t+5)dt⟩=⟨(2t+1)4+C3,−3t2+5t+C4⟩

Now, we can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that r(0)=(2,−1). Substituting t=0, we get r(0)=⟨(1)4+C3,0+0+C4⟩⟨2,−1⟩=⟨1+C3,C4⟩, so, we must have C3=1 and C4=−1. Therefore, the position vector of P at time t is r(t)=⟨(2t+1)4+1,−3t2+5t−1⟩.
